Graduate Studies Application FAQs
Ready to apply?
Read and complete all of the steps on the Apply to Study Here page before you start your application.
Apply now
Have questions? Check the frequently asked questions below or contact GPS.
Frequently Asked Questions
Username and Password
When will I receive my University of Alberta CCID (Campus Computing ID) and associated password?
You will receive your University of Alberta CCID and a temporary password within 3 days after submitting your application. The CCID and password are sent to the email address associated with your application.
Check your spam/ junk folder if you haven’t seen the email in three days. If you didn’t receive the email, or you have trouble accessing your CCID and password, please contact Information Services & Technology.
Program Eligibility
Can I apply to more than one program?
Yes. After submitting your first application, log back into your application home page and select Start New Application to apply for a second program. Please note that each application requires a separate application fee.
Can I apply for a second master’s or PhD program?
The Faculty of Graduate & Postdoctoral Studies, as well as academic departments, have different regulations regarding duplicate or secondary master’s and PhD programs. Please contact your department or program advisor for assistance.
Do I need a supervisor?
Supervisor requirements vary by program. Please consult your department’s website or program advisor for guidance.
How do I find a supervisor?
You can start by exploring the department website for the program you’re interested in. Faculty members may be listed by research area or specialization. If you need assistance looking for a supervisor please contact the department directly.
Documents and Requirements
Why are some of my documents marked with a red X?
Checklist items will show one of two statuses: Awaiting (red X) or Received (green check mark). “Awaiting” means the document has not yet been received in the Graduate Admissions Portal, while “Received” confirms that the Graduate Admissions Portal has successfully received the specific document.
Can I submit my English Language Proficiency (ELP) test score later?
Yes, you can submit your test score at a later date. However, your application will not move forward until the official score report has been received. Until then, your status will remain “Awaiting Materials”.
Can I provide unofficial documents now and submit official documents after admission?
Yes, any documents you upload yourself are considered unofficial. Official documents will be required only after you accept an admission offer and must be sent directly to the University of Alberta by the issuing institution.
What documents do I need to submit with my application?
The list of required documents, based on the information you provide, will appear in your Graduate Admissions Portal. Please log in to review your checklist.
Is there a preferred format or length for the research statement?
Requirements for research statements vary by program. Please check your department’s website or contact your program advisor for details.
Why do I need to submit a research statement if I’m applying for a course-based program?
Research statement requirements differ by program. Please visit your department’s website or reach out to your program advisor for clarification.
What if I don’t have two academic references? Or if I don’t have academic/professional references at all?
Reference requirements vary by program. Please consult your department’s website or program advisor for guidance.
Can I add or change a referee?
Yes. You can exclude a referee and add a new one. Log in to your Graduate Admissions Portal and select the Recommendations link under the Application Checklist table.
What can I do on the Reference page?
Update referee details → Edit and click Save
Add a new reference → Select Add Reference and complete the form
Send a reminder → Choose a referee and click Send Reminder (available for any referee already contacted)
Exclude a reference → Choose a referee and click Exclude (applies whether or not the referee has submitted)
Can I resend the email to my referee(s)?
Yes. You can send reminders to your listed referees directly through your Graduate Admissions Portal by selecting the Recommendations link under the Application Checklist table.
Who can I send reminders to?
Reminders can be sent to any referee who has already been contacted.
Can I change a submitted reference?
Yes. Log in to your status portal, scroll to the bottom of the Application Checklist, and select Recommendations to access the Reference page.
Can I remove a referee after I have submitted my application?
Yes. Use the Exclude option to remove them from your application.
How do I send my official documents to the University of Alberta?
Your Offer of Admission letter will indicate if you need to send official documents to the University of Alberta as part of your admission conditions. Official documents must be sent directly by the issuing organization or authority. Electronic documents can be sent to grad.transcripts@ualberta.ca, and hard copies can be sent to:
Killam Centre for Advanced Studies
2-29 Triffo Hall
University of Alberta
Edmonton, AB Canada
T6G 2E1
If the documents provided in your application are marked as official in the Graduate Admissions portal, you do not need to send duplicate documents once you are admitted.
English Language Proficiency (ELP)
Where should I have my ELP exam results sent?
For TOEFL, IELTS, and Duolingo, you cannot upload your own test scores through the Graduate Application Portal. Instead, please login to the portal of your testing organization and request that your results be sent electronically to the University of Alberta.
IELTS: Login to the IELTS booking portal to request that your scores be sent to the University of Alberta. Search for University of Alberta and select University of Alberta - Faculty of Graduate & Postdoctoral Studies.
TOEFL: Login to your TOEFL account at www.ets.org/login to request that your scores be sent to the University of Alberta. Our TOEFL code is 0963.
Duolingo: Login to your Duolingo account at englishtest.duolingo.com to request that your scores be sent to the University of Alberta. Search for University of Alberta. Once selected you will see two options: please select the Graduate option, not the Undergraduate option.
For PTE, Cambridge, or CAEL, upload a copy of your score report through the Graduate Admissions Portal. If you are admitted, you will also need to request an official copy be sent directly from the issuing organization to the University of Alberta.
Is my ELP score high enough?
Consult our English Language Proficiency (ELP) page for the minimum scores accepted for the approved English Language Proficiency Exams. Please note some departments have higher requirements than GPS.
I completed my undergraduate degree at a different university, do I have to provide an ELP test?
For information on who is required to provide an ELP, see the Recognized English Language Countries + Institutions page.
If you can’t find your previous institution and/or country in the exemption list, you will have to provide evidence of ELP via one of the methods outlined on the English Language Proficiency page.
What is a Medium of Instruction letter?
An MOI letter confirms that your previous studies were taught in English. It can be used to meet the English Language Proficiency requirement for your application.
Will the system automatically recognize my Medium of Instruction Letter?
If you meet all eligibility criteria, the system will offer you the option to select a medium of instruction letter on your application to satisfy the English Language Proficiency requirement.
Who is eligible to use a Medium of Instruction Letter to satisfy English Language Proficiency Requirements?
You qualify if:
Your program accepts Medium of Instruction letters.
Your degree level is Bachelor, Master, or PhD.
Your Academic study status is Awarded or In Progress.
The selected language of instruction for that program is English.
Your institution is not on the List of Recognized English Language Countries and Institutions (if used by your program area).
What happens if I change my selection from Medium of Instruction to another method for meeting the English Language Proficiency requirement?
If you change your mind and want to use a Medium of Instruction letter instead, your program administrator can manually add the Medium of Instruction requirement to your application.
Do all departments accept Medium of Instruction letters?
No. Some departments may still require a formal English language test. This depends on their individual admission policies.
Do I still need to upload a document if I choose the Medium of Instruction option?
Yes. If you selected the Medium of Instruction option on your application, you must upload your Medium of Instruction letter under the required document checklist. You will also be required to provide an official copy of this letter if you are admitted.
Who should I contact if I’m unsure whether I’m eligible to select "Medium of Instruction letter" to meet my English Language Proficiency requirement?
Please contact your program or department office. They can confirm your eligibility and guide you through next steps.
What is the University of Alberta's TOEFL institutional code?
The University of Alberta's institutional code is 0963.
What is the University of Alberta's IELTS institutional code?
The University of Alberta's institutional code is 190287.
You can send your ELP scores electronically by logging in to the IELTS booking portal. Select University of Alberta - Faculty of Graduate & Postdoctoral Studies.
What do I do if my ELP exam is after the application deadline?
Please contact your department directly for guidance.
I requested to have my ELP scores sent to the University of Alberta, but they haven’t received them. What should I do?
You must submit your application before you request to have your ELP scores sent to the University of Alberta.
After you submit your application, you can request to have your ELP scores sent to the University of Alberta. It can take 3-5 business days for your scores to be received and uploaded to your application.
Application Deadlines
What are the application deadlines?
Deadlines vary by program and term. Contact the department to confirm the deadlines for your program before starting your application. Find out how to contact the department by finding your program page.
Can I have an extension to the application deadline?
Deadlines for applications differ between departments and for domestic and international applications. Consult with the appropriate department for further information if you think you might miss the application deadline.
Application Fees
How much is the application fee?
A $135 CAD non-refundable application fee is required to submit your application. This fee is non-transferable.
We accept only valid Visa credit cards and Mastercard credit cards for payment. Debit cards, including Visa Debit and Mastercard Debit, are not accepted.
A non-refundable application fee is charged for each application submitted. This fee is mandatory, and we do not offer application fee waivers upon request.
Can my application fee be waived?
The application fee is mandatory. GPS does not offer application fee waivers upon request.
How can I pay the application fee if financial transactions are restricted or interrupted in my home country?
If you are unable to pay the application fee yourself, you will need to arrange for a third party to pay on your behalf using a Visa or Mastercard credit card.
Copy the secure link from the payment page in your application portal and send it to the person who has agreed to pay your application fee. Do not send this link to anyone at the University of Alberta unless you have a prearranged agreement with that individual.
Application fees can only be paid through the application portal. Debit cards, including Visa Debit and Mastercard Debit, are not accepted. Commercial third-party payment and international money transfer services are not supported. No alternative payment methods are available.
Uploading Documents
What is the difference between official and unofficial documents?
A document is considered official when it is received electronically or by mail from the issuing institution. For example, transcripts received electronically through MyCreds or ELP test results downloaded from the test centre are considered official. Hard copy transcripts and test scores that come by mail from the issuing institution/organization are also considered official.
Official documents are original or attested true copies in sealed and endorsed envelopes mailed directly from the institution/organization to the University of Alberta.
Documents submitted in support of an application become the property of the Faculty of Graduate & Postdoctoral Studies and will not subsequently be released or copied except to other U of A offices.
Unofficial documents are those that the applicant provides to the University of Alberta, either in person, by upload within the application or sent from the applicant’s email address.
Do I have to list all the schools and institutions I've attended?
Yes. You must declare all post-secondary academic records you've attended with the corresponding current transcript including completed and incomplete programs of study. This includes exchange/visiting programs and courses taken for transfer credit. Do not include: High School Education, Higher secondary education or non-credit courses taken for interest, Professional development/training, Professional designation and Continuing education courses.
My degree hasn't been conferred yet because I am still attending but I plan on finishing soon. How should I address this in my application?
Please declare all programs currently in progress by selecting the Degree Status of “in progress” and adding both the start and anticipated end date of the program. Please visit the Document Preparation page for further instructions on document preparation and submission.
When and where do I send my official documents once I have received an Offer of Admission from the U of A?
The Offer of Admission letter will provide detailed instructions on when and where to send your official documents to clear admission conditions.
I have two or more degrees from a single post-secondary institution. How do I upload these transcripts?
Please complete separate entries for each degree in the Academic History section. For example, if you completed a bachelor’s and a master’s degree both at the University of Toronto, please add one entry for the bachelor’s degree and another for the master’s degree. After you submit the application, you will see checklist items for both degrees, even if they are from the same institution. Please upload transcripts and degree certificates (if applicable) for both degrees. Your department and/or the Faculty of Graduate & Postdoctoral Studies will notify you if exceptions apply to this process during the Awaiting Materials phase.
I have applied previously and provided documents at that time. Can my old documents be used for my new application?
Applicants who attended international institutions (outside of Canada and the United States) will only need to upload their translations and degree certificates (if applicable for those institutions) the first time that they apply.
Applicants who attended domestic institutions (Canada and the United States) and who have previously submitted an application in Slate do not need to resubmit their documents, provided those documents are less than a year old.
Your department and/or the Faculty of Graduate & Postdoctoral Studies will notify you if exceptions apply to this process during the Awaiting Materials phase.
I am having trouble uploading my documents. What can I do?
Please ensure that your documents are organized based on your checklist. Each checklist item supports one document, such as a complete transcript or a degree certificate. A file that contains both the transcript and the degree certificate will not be accepted. If your transcript is saved in multiple files, it should be combined into one document before you upload it. Please remove security features, such as password protection and encryption, before you upload the documents.
If you’re applying in GSMS, the maximum size for transcripts and marksheets is 10MB, and all other documents are limited to 5MB. Please compress the file size if it exceeds 10MB. GSMS supports the upload of PDFs only.
If you are applying in the Graduate Admissions Portal, files of any type and size are permissible, within reason.
Why can’t I upload documents to my application?
You cannot upload any documents to your application until you have submitted the application form and paid the application fee.
Application Status and Timelines
How long does it take to receive a decision?
Processing times vary depending on the program you applied to.
What does “Awaiting Materials” mean?
This status means we are waiting for you to submit all required documents for your application.
What does “Awaiting Decision” mean?
This indicates you have submitted all required documents and your application is currently under review.
What does “Decided” mean?
A decision on your application has been made. Please log in to your Graduate Admissions Portal to view the outcome.
When will my application be reviewed?
Your application will be reviewed once all required documents have been submitted. The timeline for review depends on how quickly you submit your materials.
When will my checklist items show as completed?
Your checklist will be updated within 15 minutes of uploading a document. You can view the documents you uploaded in your Graduate Admissions Portal.
How do I submit my TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo scores?
Official score reports must be sent directly to the University of Alberta by the testing organization (TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo). Contact the testing office to request that your scores be sent directly to the University of Alberta.
How do I submit my PTE, Cambridge or CAEL scores?
Upload a copy of your official score report through your Graduate Admission portal. If you are admitted, you will also need to request an official copy of the report to be sent directly from the testing organization to the University of Alberta.
What else do I need to do after submitting my application?
Upon submission you will be taken to the Graduate Admission Portal, upload the required documents here.
Who can I contact about my application?
Please reach out to your department or program advisor for assistance.
Is my Application ID the same as my Slate ID?
No. Your Application ID is unique to each individual application. Your Graduate Admissions Portal ID is linked to your overall Graduate Admissions Portal profile, which may contain multiple applications.
Why haven’t I received a reply yet?
Response times vary depending on your program and application details. If additional information is needed, an admissions officer will contact you via the Graduate Admissions Portal or by email.
What is an application deadline?
The application deadline is the final date that an application can be submitted for consideration. Application deadlines vary by department and may differ for domestic and international applicants. Please check your program’s website for the most up-to-date deadline information.
Can I submit an application after the deadline?
A department may decide to accept an application after the posted deadline based on your circumstances. If you are concerned about missing a deadline, contact your department directly for guidance.
I paid for and submitted my application, but the portal still shows it as not submitted or not paid. What should I do?
It can take up to 24 hours for your application fee to be processed. Once processed, you will receive an email receipt and your application status will update automatically. If your application does not show as “Submitted” after 48 hours, please contact GPS through the Service Portal. Do not attempt to make a second payment.
How do I track the status of my application?
Log in to the Graduate Admissions Portal. Your application status will be updated there as it moves through the review process.
Can you waive the application fee?
No. Payment of the application fee is required for your application to be submitted to the University of Alberta.
Deferring Admissions
Can I defer my admission?
Deferring your offer of admission will depend on the program you’re admitted to. If the option to defer is available, you’ll find a button to request the deferral in your Graduate Admissions Portal.
How do I request a deferral?
If the option to defer is available, you’ll find a button to request the deferral in your Graduate Admissions Portal. Click the button and follow the prompts to make the request.
What is the deadline to apply for a deferral?
Contact your department to find out the last day for a deferral request.
